Why Not Others: (b) Toys and other objects also cause choking; (c) Choking is common and preventable in young children; (d) Hard sweets are a common cause of choking.

PGI Exam Trap: The choking risk of small round foods is NOT known.

5-Second Recall: Cut grapes and avoid nuts in young children.

PNC Exam Pearl: Keep small objects out of the reach of children.

question: A nurse on the ward is about to give a child an injection. Which is the MOST appropriate solution for the nurse to use to clean the skin?
option_1: Tap water from the tap
option_2: An alcohol or antiseptic wipe
option_3: Plain soap and water at the sink
option_4: The skin does NOT need cleaning
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) An alcohol or antiseptic wipe

Clinical Rationale: An alcohol or antiseptic wipe cleans the skin at the injection site and reduces the chance of infection.

Key Clue: solution used to clean the skin before an injection

Priority Principle: Skill / Procedure

Why Not Others: (a) Tap water is not an antiseptic; (c) Soap and water do not clean the skin as well as an antiseptic wipe; (d) The skin is always cleaned before an injection.

PGI Exam Trap: The skin is NOT cleaned before the injection.

5-Second Recall: Clean the skin with an alcohol or antiseptic wipe and let it dry.

PNC Exam Pearl: Use a fresh swab for each injection.

question: A nurse on the ward is caring for a child with severe acute malnutrition. Which statement about the treatment is MOST accurate?
option_1: Iron and folic acid are started at once
option_2: High energy feeds are started at once
option_3: Low sugar, low temperature and infection are treated FIRST
option_4: Fluids are restricted to reduce the swelling
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Low sugar, low temperature and infection are treated FIRST

Clinical Rationale: The dangerous problems of low sugar, low temperature and infection are treated FIRST, and only then are the feeds increased slowly.

Key Clue: treatment of severe acute malnutrition in a child

Priority Principle: Nutrition

Why Not Others: (a) Iron is added later, once the child is stable and gaining weight; (b) Sudden high energy feeding causes refeeding syndrome; (d) Fluids are not restricted in severe malnutrition.

PGI Exam Trap: Feeds are rushed in severe malnutrition.

5-Second Recall: Treat low sugar, low temperature and infection first.

PNC Exam Pearl: Build up the feeds slowly and watch for refeeding problems.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A newborn on the ward is four days old with a total bilirubin of 22 mg/dL. Which action should the nurse anticipate?
option_1: No treatment, because the level is normal
option_2: Home care with a review after a week
option_3: A change of feed and a review
option_4: An exchange transfusion as directed
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) An exchange transfusion as directed

Clinical Rationale: A bilirubin of 22 mg/dL in a four day old baby is at the level at which an exchange transfusion may be needed to protect the brain.

Key Clue: total bilirubin of 22 mg/dL at four days

Priority Principle: Lab interpretation

Why Not Others: (a) The level is far above the normal range; (b) Home care with this level risks lasting brain damage; (c) A change of feed does not treat a bilirubin this high.

PGI Exam Trap: A very high bilirubin is treated as harmless.

5-Second Recall: A very high bilirubin may need an exchange transfusion.

PNC Exam Pearl: Intensify phototherapy while preparing for the exchange.

question: A child on the ward is prescribed an oral antibiotic suspension. Which is the MOST appropriate action for the nurse to take?
option_1: Store the suspension near a heater
option_2: Use a household spoon to measure the dose
option_3: Give double the dose if one is missed
option_4: Shake the bottle and measure with the device supplied
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Shake the bottle and measure with the device supplied

Clinical Rationale: The suspension is shaken well so that the drug is mixed evenly and the dose is measured with the device supplied, so that it is accurate.

Key Clue: oral antibiotic suspension prescribed for a child

Priority Principle: Drug safety

Why Not Others: (a) Heat spoils the antibiotic; (b) Household spoons vary in size and give wrong doses; (c) Doubling a dose can be dangerous.

PGI Exam Trap: A household spoon is used to measure the suspension.

5-Second Recall: Shake the bottle and use the measuring device supplied.

PNC Exam Pearl: Store the suspension as directed on the label.

question: A nurse on the ward is caring for a child who needs an oropharyngeal airway. Which statement about the airway is MOST accurate?
option_1: It must be the correct size and is inserted by trained staff
option_2: One size fits every child in the ward
option_3: It is inserted without any measurement
option_4: It can be pushed in with force in any child
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) It must be the correct size and is inserted by trained staff

Clinical Rationale: An airway of the wrong size can block the airway or injure it, so the correct size is chosen and only trained staff insert it.

Key Clue: oropharyngeal airway in a child

Priority Principle: Concept / Airway

Why Not Others: (b) Airways come in several sizes for children; (c) The length is measured from the corner of the mouth to the angle of the jaw; (d) Forcing an airway in causes bleeding and swelling.

PGI Exam Trap: The size of the airway is NOT measured.

5-Second Recall: Measure the airway before it is inserted.

PNC Exam Pearl: Watch for vomiting and remove the airway if it occurs.

question: A nurse on the ward is preparing to resuscitate a newborn who is NOT breathing well at birth. Which is the MOST appropriate order of steps for the nurse to follow?
option_1: Start compressions before any ventilation
option_2: Dry and stimulate, open the airway, then ventilate and compress
option_3: Wait five minutes before taking any action
option_4: Give water and wait for the baby to cry
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Dry and stimulate, open the airway, then ventilate and compress

Clinical Rationale: The baby is dried and stimulated, the airway opened and ventilation given, with compressions added only if the heart rate stays very low.

Key Clue: newborn NOT breathing well at birth

Priority Principle: ABC / Newborn resuscitation

Why Not Others: (a) Compressions without ventilation do not help a newborn; (c) Waiting causes lasting damage to the brain; (d) A newborn is never given water.

PGI Exam Trap: Ventilation is delayed in the newborn.

5-Second Recall: Ventilation comes before compressions in a newborn.

PNC Exam Pearl: Assess the heart rate after every step.

question: A nurse on the ward is about to give a prescribed intravenous drug to a child. Which is the MOST appropriate order of steps for the nurse to follow?
option_1: Give the drug and check the order afterwards
option_2: Give the drug quickly without cleaning the port
option_3: Check the order, clean the port, give it slowly and flush
option_4: Use the same syringe for two different drugs
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Check the order, clean the port, give it slowly and flush

Clinical Rationale: The order and the child are checked, the port cleaned, the line flushed, the drug given slowly and the line flushed again.

Key Clue: correct sequence for an intravenous drug in a child

Priority Principle: Skill / Medication

Why Not Others: (a) The order is always checked before the drug is given; (b) An unclean port allows organisms into the blood; (d) Sharing a syringe contaminates both drugs.

PGI Exam Trap: The drug is given before the order is checked.

5-Second Recall: Give intravenous drugs slowly in a child and watch the site.

PNC Exam Pearl: Stop at once if the child cries out or the site swells.

question: A child on the ward has an intravenous infusion that has run in faster than prescribed, and the child is breathless with a cough. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Stop the infusion at once and inform the doctor
option_2: Continue the infusion at the same rate
option_3: Give a diuretic without any order
option_4: Record the finding and review the child in an hour
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Stop the infusion at once and inform the doctor

Clinical Rationale: Breathlessness with a cough after too much fluid means fluid overload, so the infusion is stopped at once and the doctor informed.

Key Clue: breathless child with a cough after an infusion ran in too fast

Priority Principle: ABC / Emergency

Why Not Others: (b) Continuing the infusion adds to the fluid overload; (c) A diuretic is given only on the doctor's order; (d) Waiting allows the lungs to fill with fluid.

PGI Exam Trap: The infusion is continued after a fluid overload.

5-Second Recall: Stop the infusion and sit the child up.

PNC Exam Pearl: Check the pump settings and the volume given.

question: An infant on the ward has an intravenous cannula in the scalp. Which is the MOST appropriate action for the nurse to take?
option_1: Cover the site with a thick bandage
option_2: Rub the site to improve the flow
option_3: Lay the infant with the head hanging down
option_4: Handle the head gently and check the site often
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Handle the head gently and check the site often

Clinical Rationale: The head is handled gently and the site checked often, because a scalp vein infusion leaks into the tissue easily.

Key Clue: infant with an intravenous cannula in the scalp

Priority Principle: Skill / Device

Why Not Others: (a) A thick bandage hides the site from view; (b) Rubbing disturbs the cannula and the vein; (c) A head down position raises the pressure in the scalp veins.

PGI Exam Trap: The scalp infusion site is NOT checked often.

5-Second Recall: Check the scalp site often for swelling.

PNC Exam Pearl: Ask the parents not to touch the cannula.

question: A newborn on the ward has a large swelling on the head after a difficult delivery. Which is the MOST appropriate action for the nurse to take?
option_1: Press firmly on the swelling to reduce it
option_2: Aspirate the swelling with a needle at once
option_3: Handle the head gently and watch the size of the swelling
option_4: Apply a tight bandage around the head
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Handle the head gently and watch the size of the swelling

Clinical Rationale: The swelling is left alone and watched, because it is absorbed over weeks and draining it risks infection and bleeding.

Key Clue: large swelling on the head of a newborn after a difficult delivery

Priority Principle: Newborn care

Why Not Others: (a) Firm pressure causes pain and may extend the bleeding; (b) Needling the swelling invites infection; (d) A tight bandage presses on the soft skull.

PGI Exam Trap: The swelling on the newborn head is needled.

5-Second Recall: Leave the swelling alone and observe it.

PNC Exam Pearl: Check for jaundice and pallor as the swelling is absorbed.

question: A nurse on the ward is advising a mother about safe sleeping for her baby. Which statement about safe sleeping to prevent cot death is MOST accurate?
option_1: The baby sleeps on the front to sleep better
option_2: The baby is placed on the back with the face clear
option_3: A pillow keeps the head in a good position
option_4: Quilts and soft toys make the cot comfortable
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) The baby is placed on the back with the face clear

Clinical Rationale: Sleeping on the back with a clear face and no pillow or soft bedding lowers the risk of cot death.

Key Clue: safe sleeping to prevent cot death

Priority Principle: Concept / Child safety

Why Not Others: (a) Sleeping on the front raises the risk; (c) A pillow is not used for a baby; (d) Soft bedding and toys can cover the face.

PGI Exam Trap: A baby is placed on the front to sleep.

5-Second Recall: Place the baby on the back to sleep.

PNC Exam Pearl: Keep the cot free of pillows, quilts and soft toys.

question: A child on the ward has opioid induced respiratory depression. Which drug should the nurse anticipate being prescribed?
option_1: Flumazenil for the sedation
option_2: N-acetylcysteine for the liver
option_3: Naloxone as prescribed
option_4: Atropine for the slow pulse
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Naloxone as prescribed

Clinical Rationale: Naloxone is an opioid antagonist that reverses the respiratory depression caused by opioid drugs.

Key Clue: drug to reverse opioid induced respiratory depression

Priority Principle: Emergency drug therapy

Why Not Others: (a) Flumazenil reverses benzodiazepines; (b) N-acetylcysteine is the antidote for paracetamol; (d) Atropine is used for organophosphate poisoning.

PGI Exam Trap: The antidotes for different poisons are confused.

5-Second Recall: Naloxone reverses opioid overdose.

PNC Exam Pearl: Support the breathing while the antidote acts.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A child on the ward develops severe diarrhoea with blood and mucus after a course of antibiotics. Which condition is the MOST likely cause?
option_1: Lactose intolerance
option_2: Simple food poisoning
option_3: A viral gastroenteritis
option_4: Antibiotic associated colitis
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Antibiotic associated colitis

Clinical Rationale: Bloody diarrhoea starting after antibiotics suggests antibiotic associated colitis, which needs isolation and urgent treatment.

Key Clue: bloody diarrhoea with mucus after a course of antibiotics

Priority Principle: Infection control

Why Not Others: (a) Lactose intolerance causes loose stools without blood; (b) Food poisoning comes on after a suspect meal and not after antibiotics; (c) Viral gastroenteritis is watery and not bloody.

PGI Exam Trap: The link with the recent antibiotic is missed.

5-Second Recall: Bloody diarrhoea after antibiotics means colitis.

PNC Exam Pearl: Use contact precautions and wash the hands with soap and water.

question: A child on the ward weighing 8 kg is prescribed 20 mg/kg/day in two divided doses. Which is the MOST appropriate dose for the nurse to give in one dose?
option_1: 80 mg
option_2: 160 mg
option_3: 40 mg
option_4: 20 mg
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) 80 mg

Clinical Rationale: Eight kilograms multiplied by twenty milligrams per kilogram gives 160 mg a day, which is halved to 80 mg for each dose.

Key Clue: child weighing 8 kg prescribed 20 mg/kg/day in two doses

Priority Principle: Drug calculation

Why Not Others: (b) 160 mg is the total for the whole day; (c) 40 mg is a quarter of the daily total; (d) 20 mg is the dose per kilogram and not the dose.

PGI Exam Trap: The daily total is used as a single dose.

5-Second Recall: Work out the daily dose and then divide by the number of doses.

PNC Exam Pearl: Check the dose against the maximum for the child's weight.

question: A child on the ward has a nose bleed. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Tilt the child's head back to stop the bleeding
option_2: Sit the child up and pinch the soft part of the nose
option_3: Lay the child flat on the floor
option_4: Send the child home without treatment
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Sit the child up and pinch the soft part of the nose

Clinical Rationale: Sitting up with the head forward and the soft part of the nose pinched stops the bleeding and keeps the blood out of the throat.

Key Clue: child with a nose bleed at school

Priority Principle: Safety / First aid

Why Not Others: (a) Tilting the head back lets blood run into the stomach; (c) Lying flat increases the bleeding; (d) Untreated bleeding continues.

PGI Exam Trap: The head is tilted back for a nose bleed.

5-Second Recall: Sit up, lean forward and pinch the soft part of the nose.

PNC Exam Pearl: Hold the pressure for ten minutes without letting go.

question: A nurse on the ward is about to do a heel prick on a newborn for blood screening. Which is the MOST appropriate order of steps for the nurse to follow?
option_1: Prick the skin without cleaning it FIRST
option_2: Squeeze the heel hard to get the blood out
option_3: Prick the centre of the heel for the sample
option_4: Warm the heel, prick the outer side and collect the blood
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Warm the heel, prick the outer side and collect the blood

Clinical Rationale: The heel is warmed and cleaned, the outer side pricked to avoid the bone, the blood collected on the card and the bleeding stopped with pressure.

Key Clue: correct sequence for a heel prick on a newborn

Priority Principle: Skill / Procedure

Why Not Others: (a) Cleaning the skin prevents infection; (b) Hard squeezing damages the tissues and gives a poor sample; (c) The centre of the heel is over the bone and must be avoided.

PGI Exam Trap: The centre of the heel is pricked.

5-Second Recall: Prick the outer side of the heel and avoid the bone.

PNC Exam Pearl: Fill the circles on the card completely and let them dry.

question: A health worker who visits the village notices a child with bow legs, beaded ribs and a large soft skull. Which deficiency is the MOST likely cause?
option_1: Vitamin D deficiency
option_2: Vitamin A deficiency
option_3: Iron deficiency
option_4: Vitamin C deficiency
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Vitamin D deficiency

Clinical Rationale: Bow legs, beaded ribs and a large soft skull are the bone signs of rickets, which is caused by a lack of vitamin D.

Key Clue: bow legs, beaded ribs and a large soft skull in a child

Priority Principle: Community assessment

Why Not Others: (b) Vitamin A deficiency causes eye problems; (c) Iron deficiency causes pallor and tiredness; (d) Vitamin C deficiency causes bleeding gums and painful joints.

PGI Exam Trap: The bone signs of rickets are NOT recognised.

5-Second Recall: Rickets causes bow legs and beaded ribs.

PNC Exam Pearl: Advise sunlight exposure and give vitamin D as prescribed.

question: A child on the ward with type 1 diabetes is on insulin. Which finding is the MOST likely to show that the treatment is working?
option_1: Frequent low sugars with poor growth
option_2: Normal growth with a steady weight and few low sugars
option_3: A high blood sugar with weight loss
option_4: Frequent infections with slow healing
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Normal growth with a steady weight and few low sugars

Clinical Rationale: Steady growth and weight with few hypoglycaemic episodes show that the insulin and the diet are well balanced.

Key Clue: child with type one diabetes on insulin

Priority Principle: Paediatric care

Why Not Others: (a) Frequent low sugars with poor growth means the control is poor; (c) A high sugar with weight loss means the insulin is not enough; (d) Frequent infections suggest poor long term control.

PGI Exam Trap: Growth and low sugars are NOT used to judge control.

5-Second Recall: Judge control by growth, weight and low sugars.

PNC Exam Pearl: Teach the family to recognise and treat hypoglycaemia.

question: A child on the ward has a wound that is bleeding. Which is the MOST appropriate action for the nurse to take?
option_1: Pour water over the wound continuously
option_2: Apply a loose dressing without any pressure
option_3: Apply firm direct pressure with a clean pad
option_4: Apply a tourniquet to the limb at once
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Apply firm direct pressure with a clean pad

Clinical Rationale: Firm direct pressure with a clean pad over the bleeding point controls the bleeding and is the FIRST step.

Key Clue: bleeding wound in a child

Priority Principle: First aid

Why Not Others: (a) Continuous washing does not control bleeding; (b) A dressing without pressure does not stop the bleeding; (d) A tourniquet is a last resort when pressure fails.

PGI Exam Trap: A loose dressing is applied to a bleeding wound.

5-Second Recall: Apply firm direct pressure to a bleeding wound.

PNC Exam Pearl: Wash the wound under running water once the bleeding has stopped.

question: A child on the ward taking medicine for epilepsy has more fits after two days of missed doses. Which is the MOST appropriate action for the nurse to take?
option_1: Double the dose without any advice from the doctor
option_2: Inform the doctor at once and restart the drug as prescribed
option_3: Stop the drug altogether and watch the child
option_4: Give a sedative to settle the child down
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Inform the doctor at once and restart the drug as prescribed

Clinical Rationale: Missed doses of an antiepileptic cause breakthrough fits, so the doctor is informed and the drug restarted exactly as prescribed.

Key Clue: more fits after two days of missed antiepileptic doses

Priority Principle: Drug safety

Why Not Others: (a) Doubling the dose without an order is dangerous; (c) Stopping the drug causes more fits; (d) A sedative does not treat the missed doses.

PGI Exam Trap: The missed doses are NOT linked with the fits.

5-Second Recall: Restart the antiepileptic as prescribed.

PNC Exam Pearl: Teach the family not to miss doses.

question: A child on the ward has chickenpox. Which statement about the spread of chickenpox is MOST accurate?
option_1: It spreads through food and drinking water
option_2: It spreads after the rash has appeared and NOT before the rash
option_3: It spreads by droplets and contact and is infectious before the rash
option_4: It is NOT infectious to other children at all
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) It spreads by droplets and contact and is infectious before the rash

Clinical Rationale: Chickenpox spreads by droplets and direct contact and the child is infectious for a day or two before the rash appears.

Key Clue: spread of chickenpox

Priority Principle: Concept / Infection

Why Not Others: (a) It does not spread through food and water; (b) The child is infectious before the rash appears; (d) It is highly infectious.

PGI Exam Trap: The infectious period of chickenpox is NOT known.

5-Second Recall: Chickenpox is infectious before the rash.

PNC Exam Pearl: Isolate the child until all the crusts have formed.

question: A child on the ward has a suspected airway foreign body and is coughing forcefully. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Lay the child flat on the floor
option_2: Give back blows at once to clear it
option_3: Give abdominal thrusts at once
option_4: Encourage the child to keep coughing and stay ready
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Encourage the child to keep coughing and stay ready

Clinical Rationale: A forceful cough means the airway is only partly blocked and coughing is the BEST way to clear it, so the nurse stays ready to help.

Key Clue: child with a suspected airway foreign body who is coughing forcefully

Priority Principle: ABC / Emergency

Why Not Others: (a) Lying flat does not help to clear the airway; (b) Back blows are used when the cough becomes weak or silent; (c) Abdominal thrusts are not used while the cough is effective.

PGI Exam Trap: An effective cough is interrupted by back blows.

5-Second Recall: Encourage coughing while the cough is strong.

PNC Exam Pearl: Start back blows and thrusts if the cough becomes silent.

question: A child on the ward has been treated for dehydration. Which finding is the MOST likely to show that the child is fully rehydrated?
option_1: A stable weight with a moist mouth and good urine output
option_2: A dry mouth with a slow skin pinch on the abdomen
option_3: Sunken eyes with drowsiness in the child
option_4: A fall in weight with no urine passed at all
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) A stable weight with a moist mouth and good urine output

Clinical Rationale: A stable weight with normal skin turgor, a moist mouth and a good urine output all show that the fluid has been replaced.

Key Clue: finding that shows full rehydration in a child

Priority Principle: Paediatric care

Why Not Others: (b) A dry mouth with a slow skin pinch means dehydration continues; (c) Sunken eyes with drowsiness means severe dehydration; (d) Weight loss with no urine shows the fluid is not enough.

PGI Exam Trap: Continuing dehydration is read as full rehydration.

5-Second Recall: Use weight, skin turgor, mouth and urine output together.

PNC Exam Pearl: Count the wet nappies over the day.

question: A nurse on the ward has four children to care for, including a child with noisy breathing. Which child should the nurse see FIRST?
option_1: A child with noisy breathing and a blue tinge round the lips
option_2: A child waiting for a routine dressing change
option_3: A child whose mother wants feeding advice
option_4: A child who is due for a routine medicine
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) A child with noisy breathing and a blue tinge round the lips

Clinical Rationale: Noisy breathing with a blue tinge means the airway is threatened, so that child is seen before all the others.

Key Clue: which of four children should be seen FIRST

Priority Principle: Management / Priority

Why Not Others: (b) A routine dressing can wait; (c) Advice about feeding can wait; (d) A routine medicine can be given shortly afterwards.

PGI Exam Trap: Airway problems are NOT given the highest priority.

5-Second Recall: Airway, breathing and circulation come first.

PNC Exam Pearl: Ask for help at once when a child is deteriorating.

question: A child on the ward has an intravenous infusion running. Which is the MOST appropriate action for the nurse to take?
option_1: Check the infusion at the end of the shift
option_2: Check the rate, the site and the volume at intervals
option_3: Allow the parents to adjust the rate
option_4: Increase the rate when the child cries
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Check the rate, the site and the volume at intervals

Clinical Rationale: The rate, the site and the volume given are checked regularly, so that the right amount is given and any problem at the site is found early.

Key Clue: child with an intravenous infusion running

Priority Principle: Skill / Device

Why Not Others: (a) Checking only at the end of the shift may miss a serious change; (c) Only the nurse adjusts the rate; (d) The rate is set by the prescription and not by crying.

PGI Exam Trap: The infusion rate is adjusted to settle the child.

5-Second Recall: Check the rate and the site regularly.

PNC Exam Pearl: Use a pump or burette to control the volume in a child.

question: A child on the ward has a temperature of 40 degrees Celsius. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Wrap the child in warm blankets
option_2: Wait for the next round of observations to be taken
option_3: Give the prescribed antipyretic and start tepid sponging
option_4: Give the child a cold bath at once
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Give the prescribed antipyretic and start tepid sponging

Clinical Rationale: A temperature of 40 degrees is treated at once with the prescribed antipyretic and tepid sponging to bring it down safely.

Key Clue: child with a temperature of 40 degrees Celsius

Priority Principle: Priority / Care

Why Not Others: (a) Warm blankets raise the temperature; (b) Waiting allows the temperature to rise further; (d) A cold bath causes shivering and a further rise.

PGI Exam Trap: A high fever is left untreated until the next round.

5-Second Recall: Treat a high fever at once and recheck the temperature.

PNC Exam Pearl: Look for the cause of the fever as well.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A child on the ward who was well yesterday now has a high fever, is drooling and sits forward refusing to swallow. Which condition is the MOST likely cause?
option_1: A simple sore throat
option_2: Tonsillitis
option_3: Croup
option_4: Acute epiglottitis
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Acute epiglottitis

Clinical Rationale: A high fever with drooling and sitting forward refusing to swallow points to acute epiglottitis, which is an airway emergency.

Key Clue: high fever with drooling and sitting forward refusing to swallow

Priority Principle: ABC / Emergency

Why Not Others: (a) A simple sore throat does not cause drooling; (b) Tonsillitis causes a sore throat without drooling; (c) Croup causes a barking cough with stridor.

PGI Exam Trap: The airway emergency of epiglottitis is missed.

5-Second Recall: Drooling with a high fever means epiglottitis.

PNC Exam Pearl: Do not examine the throat and keep the child calm and upright.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).
